Challenges include the rapid pace of technological change and the need for significant investments in monitoring and infrastructure.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has launched the IT Resilience Index (ITRI), a quantitative tool to assess the robustness of technology systems in market infrastructure institutions (MIIs). The index aims to evaluate the ability of MIIs, such as stock exchanges and clearing corporations, to handle operational shocks, cyber threats, and technical failures. SEBI's ITRI is based on nine weighted parameters, with availability and security given the highest priority. The initiative reflects a shift from compliance-based oversight to risk-monitoring frameworks, aligning with global trends in operational resilience. However, challenges remain, including the rapid pace of technological change and the need for substantial investments in automated monitoring systems. SEBI's ITRI could serve as a global model for future-ready financial architecture if implemented effectively.
items.title: SEBI Introduces ITRI to Measure Financial Market Technology Resilience

key_points: Wolf attacks on livestock in Mahuadanr Sanctuary peak at night and early morning, during winter and early summer, and near forest edges.
Over half of surveyed households reported livestock losses, with 415 goats killed and an estimated economic loss of ₹21 lakhs.

Tribal communities tolerate wolves despite livestock losses, viewing them as part of the natural landscape.
The study recommends predator-proof enclosures, improved livestock management, and protecting denning habitats to reduce conflict.
items.summary: A study from India's first wolf sanctuary, Mahuadanr in Jharkhand, found that wolf attacks on livestock are most likely at night and early morning, during winter and early summer, and near forest edges. Over half of surveyed households reported livestock losses, with 415 goats killed and an estimated economic loss of ₹21 lakhs. Researchers identified ecological and socio-economic factors influencing attacks, noting that proximity to the sanctuary boundary increased losses. Despite significant livestock depredation, many tribal communities tolerate wolves, viewing them as part of the natural landscape. The study recommends targeted mitigation strategies, including predator-proof enclosures and improved livestock management, to reduce conflict while supporting conservation efforts.
items.title: Study from India’s first wolf sanctuary reveals when livestock are most at risk

key_points: A man accused of harassment and blackmailing a family whose three members died in the Godavari River has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh.
The family members, including an engineer and his wife, died near the Road-cum-Rail Bridge in Rajamahendravaram, with their 10-year-old grandson rescued.
Police allege the accused threatened and blackmailed the family using private videos, with a suicide note accusing him of poisoning the husband and staging his death as a suicide.
Six teams have been formed to investigate the case, including examining the suicide notes and the circumstances of the family's deaths.
A former MP has called for a CBI or NIA probe, alleging a wider conspiracy and international links.
items.summary: A man accused of harassing and blackmailing a family whose three members died after jumping into the Godavari River in Andhra Pradesh has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh. Shaik Sadiq Khan, the accused, was arrested in Meerut on August 22 following a multi-state search. The family members, including an engineer and his wife, died near the Road-cum-Rail Bridge in Rajamahendravaram. Their 10-year-old grandson was rescued. Police allege Khan harassed the family, threatened them, and blackmailed them using private videos. A suicide note from the daughter accused Khan of poisoning her husband and making his death appear a suicide. Khan is also linked to a separate murder case. Authorities have formed six teams to investigate the case, which includes examining the suicide notes and the circumstances surrounding the family's deaths. A former MP has called for a CBI or NIA probe, alleging a wider conspiracy and international links.
items.title: Engineer's family dies in Godavari; suspect arrested in UP

key_points: The Allahabad High Court rejected a student's claim that wearing a headscarf is an essential religious practice for constitutional protection.
The court stated that the petition lacked the necessary factual and legal foundation to support the assertion.
The school's uniform policy was upheld as a legitimate institutional rule, not discriminatory.
Muslim clerics criticized the ruling, arguing that hijab is an integral part of Islam and should be allowed within school dress codes.
The case underscores the court's requirement for clear evidence to establish religious practices as essential for constitutional claims.
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court dismissed a petition from a student who sought to continue wearing a headscarf with her school uniform in Class 11. The student had worn the scarf since Class 6 without prior objection, but the school refused admission, citing its dress code. The court ruled that the claim of the headscarf being an essential religious practice was a 'bare assertion' lacking necessary factual and legal foundation. It emphasized that schools have the authority to enforce uniform policies as part of their disciplinary framework, provided they are applied without discrimination. The judgment drew criticism from Muslim clerics, who argued that hijab is an integral part of Islam and should be permitted within school dress codes. The court's decision highlights the distinction between institutional rules and constitutional claims, rejecting the petition on the grounds that it failed to meet the required legal standards.
items.title: Allahabad High Court Rules Headscarf Not Essential Religious Practice for Constitutional Claim

key_points: Israeli strikes at Nasser Hospital in Gaza killed 22 people, including journalists, with no accountability sought one year later.
An anonymous Israeli soldier claims the military found no evidence linking the targeted camera to Hamas, contradicting official statements.
The Israeli military has not provided details about its investigation or a timeline, despite repeated requests from The Associated Press.
Rights groups and journalists criticize Israel’s pattern of retroactive incrimination of Palestinians, raising concerns about transparency and accountability.
The strikes, involving four tank shell attacks, have raised questions about the military’s rationale and potential war crimes, including accusations of a 'double tap' attack on first responders.
items.summary: One year after Israeli strikes killed 22 people, including journalists, at Nasser Hospital in Gaza, no one has been held accountable. The attacks, which occurred on August 25, 2025, targeted a suspected Hamas camera on the hospital roof, but subsequent investigations have failed to confirm militant links among the victims. An anonymous Israeli soldier reported that the military found no evidence connecting the camera, belonging to Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri, to Hamas. The soldier also claimed none of the six individuals identified as Hamas-linked were the intended targets. The Israeli military has not provided details about its investigation or a timeline for completion, despite repeated requests from The Associated Press. Rights groups and journalists have criticized Israel’s lack of accountability, noting a pattern of retroactive incrimination of Palestinians. The strikes, which involved four tank shell attacks, resulted in the deaths of 33-year-old AP journalist Mariam Dagga and others, raising questions about the military’s rationale and potential war crimes. AP and Reuters have called for transparency and access to Gaza for journalists covering the conflict.
items.title: Israeli strikes at Gaza hospital killed journalists; accountability remains elusive

items.summary: iranian security forces used mosques across tehran as bases to monitor and confront protesters during a deadly crackdown in january, according to evidence obtained by iran international. intercepted communications, video footage, and eyewitness accounts show security personnel operating from several mosques, including imam hossein mosque, to deploy forces and equipment. witnesses described security activity around mosques after electricity was cut, with drones flying overhead. the report suggests some mosques functioned as operational bases rather than just places of worship. the crackdown occurred amid widespread protests in iran, which have since been overshadowed by the broader conflict involving iran, israel, and the united states. washington has shifted toward economic pressure, with new sanctions against iran-linked entities and warnings to countries doing business with tehran. iran's rial has fallen to a record low, adding to economic strain, while pakistan has sent a delegation to encourage negotiations between washington and tehran.

items.summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian firms for facilitating the import of Iranian petrochemical products, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at cutting Iran's financial lifelines. key_points: The Supreme Court will form a special bench to assess the application of its March 11 OBC creamy-layer judgment to the 2025 civil services exam.

The Department of Personnel and Training seeks permission to allocate services to 958 candidates under the previous creamy-layer rules.
The government contends that candidates who applied under the old administrative interpretation may have acted on the legal position in force at the time.
The court will consider setting up a special bench to address these concerns, with the government seeking clarity on the judgment's application to the completed process.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to form a special bench to examine whether its March 11 judgment on OBC creamy-layer criteria applies to the 2025 civil services exam. The Centre argues that applying the ruling to the completed selection process could lead to unequal treatment of candidates and delay training and cadre allocation. The Department of Personnel and Training seeks permission to allocate services to 958 candidates recommended under the previous creamy-layer rules. The government contends that candidates who applied under the old administrative interpretation may have acted on the legal position in force at the time, and a retrospective application of the judgment could create disparities. The court will consider setting up a special bench to address these concerns, with the government seeking clarity on the judgment's application to the completed process.
items.title: Supreme Court may form special bench on OBC quota rules for civil services exam

items.summary: Human Rights Watch reports that Colombian drug gangs and rebel groups are recruiting children through social media to pilot explosive drones, marking a shift in their tactics. The report highlights that at least 1,500 children have been recruited since 2021, with 625 cases reported in 2024 alone. Armed groups are using platforms like Meta and TikTok to lure children, with algorithms potentially promoting content that encourages recruitment. HRW verified videos of children operating drones and noted that some commanders presented drone use as a game. The report also found that nearly half of the recruited children are Indigenous, and girls make up 40% of the cases. HRW urges the Colombian government to strengthen protections and hold recruiters accountable, while calling on social media companies to improve reporting tools.
items.title: Colombian drug gangs use social media to recruit children for drone operations

items.summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian companies for importing petroleum and petrochemical products from Iran, according to the State Department. The firms include Portease Partners LLP and its partners, Sadashiva Overseas Limited, PP Softtech Private Limited, and Prakrutees Infra Impex Private Limited. The sanctions, part of Operation Economic Outcast, aim to cut off Iran's financial lifelines by targeting its oil revenue. The companies were listed for knowingly engaging in transactions involving Iranian petroleum products, with Sadashiva Overseas importing $69 million worth of goods. The Treasury Secretary described the campaign as unprecedented, seeking to pressure Iran into changing its policies through economic measures.

key_points: India's DGCA is considering expanding annual random drug tests for all 12,000 commercial pilots, potentially making it the first country with such a policy.

items.summary: India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is considering expanding drug testing for commercial pilots from 10% to 100% annual random testing, potentially making it the first country with such a policy. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu stated that the proposal aims to enhance safety but acknowledges the operational challenges for airlines. The move follows an incident where an Air India pilot tested positive for narcotics, prompting one-time testing of all pilots. Airlines would need to manage increased testing volumes, infrastructure, and crew downtime. While some airlines already conduct higher testing rates, the DGCA is assessing the balance between safety improvements and operational feasibility. The Federation of Indian Pilots supports expanded testing but advocates for a gradual increase and the use of oral-fluid testing alongside urine-based methods.
items.title: India Considers Annual Random Drug Tests for All Airline Pilots

key_points: The ex-mill price of sugar fell 18% to ₹55/kg after government intervention to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding.

Government measures, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices.
Wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg, with gaps of ₹2-3/kg and ₹7-8/kg respectively between ex-mill and these levels.
items.summary: The ex-mill price of sugar dropped 18% to ₹55 per kg following government measures to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding, according to Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra. Prices had previously surged to ₹67/kg due to mills increasing rates, which Chopra attributed to non-fundamental factors. The government's actions, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices. While ex-mill prices are expected to fall further, wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg respectively. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories noted a ₹2-3/kg gap between ex-mill and wholesale prices, and a ₹7-8/kg gap between ex-mill and retail prices.
items.title: Government intervention lowers sugar ex-mill prices to ₹55/kg, curbing speculation and hoarding

They seek an immediate stay on the August 12 notification, warning of economic hardship for thousands of drivers.
The case is scheduled for urgent consideration on August 26.
items.summary: Four app-based cab drivers in Mumbai have filed a petition with the Bombay High Court challenging Maharashtra's new rule requiring Marathi language proficiency for auto-rickshaw, taxi, and app-based drivers. Petitioners claim nearly 9.65 lakh permits and badges have been issued, with many drivers unable to speak Marathi. items.title: Mumbai drivers challenge Marathi language rule in court, citing livelihood risks

Chowta criticized Karnataka's silence on the decision, despite its direct impact on the state, and called for public endorsement of the August 21 notification.

Shivakumar to support the Railway Ministry's decision to integrate Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway (SWR). Chowta emphasized that the move aligns with Karnataka's developmental needs and allows for more integrated planning of rail networks. It argues that Modi's public image, or 'front stage' self, is carefully constructed and lacks the authenticity seen in Singh's work. Stories include women who fled conflict, carrying objects that symbolize their past and serve as a connection to their homeland.
The exhibition underscores the often-overlooked labor of women in migration, who rebuild domestic life and preserve cultural practices.
The organizers argue that displacement involves more than movement, encompassing the act of carrying memory and maintaining connections to the past.
items.summary: An exhibition titled 'What Women Carry' explores the personal items women take when leaving home, highlighting their significance in migration and memory. The display includes photographs and handwritten accounts of objects like jewelry, clothing, and heirlooms, connected by red threads to form a narrative of loss and continuity. Organized by the Margins to Access Project, the exhibition features stories of women who fled conflict, violence, or economic hardship, carrying fragments of their past with them. One woman described wearing a necklace as a connection to her homeland, while others carried items with emotional weight, such as a dress from Myanmar or shirts belonging to a deceased husband. The exhibition emphasizes the often-overlooked labor of women in migration, who rebuild domestic life and preserve cultural practices. The organizers argue that displacement is not just about movement but also about carrying memory and maintaining connections to the past.
items.title: Exhibition captures women's personal belongings as symbols of displacement and memory

key_points: A study found that over 70% of ornamental plants sold online in India are alien species, many of which are invasive or naturalised in other countries.
57 invasive species already declared harmful in India are still available for purchase online, highlighting biosecurity gaps.
The online ornamental plant trade increases propagule pressure and geographic spread, bypassing biosecurity checkpoints.
Researchers suggest implementing risk-assessment protocols, public awareness campaigns, and regulatory measures to mitigate invasion risks.
A screening tool based on 'invasive elsewhere' metrics is proposed to prioritise species for further evaluation.
items.summary: A study published in Environmental Conservation reveals that a majority of ornamental plants sold online in India are alien species, many of which are invasive or naturalised in other countries. Researchers analyzed data from three major online retailers and found 1,371 out of 1,856 species were alien, with 327 classified as invasive elsewhere. The study highlights biosecurity gaps, noting that 57 invasive species already declared harmful in India are still available for purchase. Lead author Kesang Bhutia explains that ornamental plants often escape cultivation and naturalise, posing ecological risks. The online trade, facilitated by e-commerce platforms, increases propagule pressure and geographic spread, bypassing biosecurity checkpoints. The authors suggest implementing risk-assessment protocols, public awareness campaigns, and regulatory measures to mitigate invasion risks. They also propose a screening tool based on 'invasive elsewhere' metrics to prioritise species for further evaluation.
items.title: Online ornamental plant trade in India includes many invasive species

key_points: IBM released two new speech recognition models, Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC, with 470M parameters and high accuracy.

They differ in training data and licensing, with the noncommercial model scoring slightly better accuracy on most tests.
The encoder-only design provides faster throughput and a smaller memory footprint compared to previous models.
The models use a lower token rate and different tokenizations, with training data including natural and synthetic datasets.
items.summary: IBM has released two new speech recognition models, Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC, which offer high accuracy and unprecedented speed. The models, with 470M parameters, achieve over 12,600 RTFx on an NVIDIA H200 GPU, enabling transcription of more than 3.5 hours of speech in one second. They differ in training data and licensing: one uses a CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license with additional data, while the other is Apache 2.0 licensed. Both models perform well on public and far-field speech recognition benchmarks, with the noncommercial model scoring 4.85% WER and the Apache 2.0 model 5.00% WER. The encoder-only design provides faster throughput and a smaller memory footprint compared to previous models, though it sacrifices some capabilities like speech translation. The models use a lower token rate and different tokenizations, with training data including natural and synthetic datasets.
items.title: IBM Releases Fast and Accurate Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC Models

items.summary: NVIDIA introduces CUDA Python 1.0, a unified framework enabling direct access to the full CUDA platform from Python. This release includes libraries like cuda.core, which provides Pythonic interfaces to CUDA runtime, and cuda.bindings, offering low-level C API access. The new system replaces fragmented approaches where developers had to choose between low-level CUDA C++ or higher-level libraries like PyTorch. CUDA Python 1.0 introduces semantic versioning, ensuring API stability and reducing version conflicts. It enables libraries to share resources across the ecosystem, allowing features like green contexts and inter-process memory sharing. The release aims to simplify GPU development by providing a common foundation for all Python-based CUDA applications, reducing the need for custom bindings and improving interoperability between libraries such as CuPy and PyTorch.
items.title: CUDA Python 1.0 Unifies GPU Access for Python Developers

key_points: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) enables a 4-bit compressed model to outperform its full-precision bfloat16 version on 7 of 9 benchmarks.
QAH distills knowledge directly from the original, pre-compression model rather than from a recovered checkpoint, avoiding degradation from a degraded teacher.
The 4-bit model uses less memory and compute, making it cheaper to run while maintaining or improving accuracy.
QAH reaches peak performance faster than quantization-aware training (QAT) and maintains stability, reducing deployment risks.
The method was tested on a GPT-OSS 120B model, showing gains in long-context reasoning and math tasks, with the largest gains on capabilities typically damaged by compression.
items.summary: A new method called Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) allows a 4-bit compressed model to outperform its full-precision bfloat16 version on 7 of 9 benchmarks, according to a paper by Multiverse Computing. The approach distills knowledge directly from the original, pre-compression model rather than from a recovered checkpoint, enabling the 4-bit model to surpass its 16-bit counterpart in accuracy and efficiency. QAH achieves this by using KL divergence on output logits, avoiding the instability of cross-entropy loss. The 4-bit model also uses less memory and compute, making it cheaper to run. The method was tested on a GPT-OSS 120B model compressed to 60B parameters, showing significant gains in long-context reasoning and math tasks. Compared to quantization-aware training (QAT), QAH reaches peak performance faster and maintains stability, reducing deployment risks. The research highlights how compression and quantization can be combined to create more efficient models without sacrificing capabilities.
items.title: Quantization-Aware Healing Enables 4-Bit Model to Outperform Full-Precision Original

items.summary: STARFlow2 combines language models and normalizing flows to enable continuous, single-pass multimodal generation. The model uses a Pretzel architecture that interleaves a frozen vision-language model with a TARFlow stream, operating under the same causal mask. This design preserves pretrained understanding, allows high-fidelity image generation, and supports cache-friendly interleaved output. Experiments show strong performance in image generation and multimodal understanding. The work highlights autoregressive flows as a foundation for unified modeling.
items.title: STARFlow2 integrates language models and flows for unified multimodal generation

The agent supports multiple models, including Qwen 3.8 27B and PPLX 27B, with plans to add Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Perplexity emphasizes that local AI avoids data breaches and eliminates cloud-related costs, though the current hardware requirements may limit accessibility.

key_points: Linus Torvalds introduced Linux in 1991 as a personal project, nearly naming it 'Freax' before settling on 'Linux.'
The project began with a Usenet post and grew through collaborative development, with early contributors like Theodore Ts'o playing key roles.
The adoption of the GNU Public License version 2 in 1992 was a critical step in Linux's widespread use.
Torvalds remains actively involved in Linux, viewing it as a significant milestone in software development.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: Linus Torvalds, a Finnish graduate student, introduced Linux in 1991 as a hobby project, initially intending to name it 'Freax'—a blend of 'free,' 'freak,' and 'x.' However, his friend Ari Lemmke disliked the name, leading to the adoption of 'Linux.' The project started with a Usenet post on August 25, 1991, and quickly gained traction through collaborative development. Torvalds emphasized that Linux's growth was gradual and unexpected, with early contributors like Theodore Ts'o helping expand its reach. The shift to the GNU Public License version 2 in 1992 was pivotal, enabling Linux's widespread adoption. Torvalds remains actively involved, viewing Linux as a significant cultural and technical milestone in software development.
items.title: Linus Torvalds' Linux began as a hobby, nearly named Freax

key_points: Schneier and Rafi argue AI lacks the ability to develop substantial new mathematical theories.
AI has produced notable results, such as disproving conjectures and finding novel applications of existing techniques.
The authors highlight AI's strength in recombining ideas but note its limitations in deep conceptual innovation.
They remain optimistic about future AI capabilities in mathematical creativity despite current limitations.
items.summary: Mathematicians Bruce Schneier and Kasra Rafi argue that while AI has produced notable mathematical results, it currently lacks the ability to develop substantial new conceptual frameworks. They note AI models have disproven conjectures and found novel applications of existing techniques, but these achievements do not equate to true mathematical creativity. The authors emphasize that AI excels at recombining existing ideas but struggles with deep, sustained theory-building. They acknowledge AI's growing capabilities but caution that significant conceptual innovation remains beyond its current reach, though they remain optimistic about future developments.
items.title: Mathematicians Discuss AI's Role in Their Field

key_points: A 2026 CyberArk survey found 91% of organizations maintain always-on privileged access, creating a high-risk environment for AI agents.
Three separate disclosures showed that sanctioned AI agents inherit permissions from their host environments, leading to potential exploitation.
Unsanctioned 'shadow AI' tools, used by 45% of employees, access internal data and execute commands without oversight, increasing the risk of data exfiltration.
Sysdig documented the first end-to-end AI-agent-driven ransomware attack, exploiting known vulnerabilities and persistent credentials.
The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications now includes risks like identity abuse and unexpected code execution, urging better governance of AI agent access.
items.summary: In early 2026, a series of vulnerabilities and a landmark incident shifted AI security from theoretical concerns to real infrastructure compromises. A CyberArk survey revealed that 91% of organizations maintain always-on privileged access, creating an environment where AI agents operate with broad permissions and minimal oversight. Three separate disclosures showed that sanctioned agents inherit permissions from their host environments, leading to potential exploitation. Meanwhile, unsanctioned 'shadow AI' tools, used by 45% of employees, compounded the risk by accessing internal data and executing commands without oversight. The Sysdig Threat Research Team documented the first end-to-end AI-agent-driven ransomware attack, exploiting known vulnerabilities and persistent credentials. The incident highlighted the need for just-in-time access controls, better discovery of nonhuman identities, and stronger governance frameworks. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications now includes these risks, urging organizations to treat agent access as an identity lifecycle issue with the same rigor as human access management.
items.title: AI Agents Exploit Persistent Privileges in 2026 Cybersecurity Breach

key_points: NVIDIA outlines a framework for full-stack observability to detect silent failures in AI infrastructure.
The framework maps AI components to telemetry tools and emphasizes selecting the minimum necessary tools to cover failure domains.
A unified triage dashboard is recommended, integrating metrics from DCGM, NVSM, UFM, and BCM.
The article advocates for a two-layer monitoring approach to streamline triage and detailed analysis.
Observability maturity should be measured by actionable signals, not the number of dashboards.
items.summary: NVIDIA provides a framework for implementing full-stack observability in AI infrastructure to detect and resolve silent failures. The article explains how to map AI components to telemetry tools, select the right monitoring stack, and create a unified triage dashboard. It highlights the importance of focusing on key metrics and avoiding alert fatigue by prioritizing signals that directly inform remediation actions. The framework emphasizes a step-by-step approach, starting with essential tools like DCGM, NVSM, and UFM, and expanding coverage as needed. NVIDIA also recommends a two-layer monitoring system for efficient troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.
items.title: NVIDIA Outlines Observability Strategy for AI Infrastructure

key_points: NVIDIA has introduced open world models like Cosmos 3 to enhance physical AI capabilities.
Cosmos 3 enables developers to generate training data, simulate environments, and specialize models for robotics and autonomous vehicles.
The models are available under the Linux Foundation’s OpenMDW 1.1 license, allowing post-training on custom data and hardware.
Cosmos 3 offers variants for different use cases, including high-fidelity world modeling and on-device vision reasoning.
NVIDIA’s physical AI stack includes tools and a coalition to foster collaboration in developing open world models.
items.summary: NVIDIA has introduced open world models, such as Cosmos 3, to advance physical AI by enabling developers to generate training data, simulate environments, and specialize models for robotics, autonomous vehicles, and vision AI. These models, available under the Linux Foundation’s OpenMDW 1.1 license, allow teams to post-train on their own data and hardware. Cosmos 3, built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture, combines vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction, offering variants for different use cases. NVIDIA’s physical AI stack includes tools like Isaac GR00T, Alpamayo, and Metropolis, while the NVIDIA Cosmos Coalition fosters collaboration across industries to develop open world models for various applications.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Open World Models for Physical AI Applications

key_points: MIT students participated in the JARVIS Challenge to test AI's role in designing and building a jet engine.
AI was used for various tasks, including design, documentation, and vendor sourcing, but faced limitations in physical understanding and vendor coordination.
Human expertise and hands-on experience were critical for successful engine testing, with the winning team relying more on traditional engineering principles.
The competition showed that while AI can enhance productivity, human judgment and fundamental knowledge remain essential for safety-critical systems.
The JARVIS Challenge emphasized the importance of balancing AI use with human expertise in engineering education and practice.
items.summary: MIT undergraduates participated in the JARVIS Challenge, a four-week competition to design and build a small gas turbine jet engine using AI as a primary engineering tool. The challenge aimed to explore whether AI could accelerate the design-build-test cycle for complex physical systems. Teams used AI for tasks like summarizing textbooks, creating designs, and sourcing vendors, but faced limitations in areas requiring physical understanding and vendor coordination. While AI aided in initial design phases, human expertise and hands-on experience proved critical for successful engine testing. The competition highlighted that AI can enhance engineering productivity, but human judgment and fundamental knowledge remain essential for safety-critical systems. The winning team, 811 Crew, relied more on traditional engineering principles and teamwork, demonstrating that a balance between AI use and human expertise is key to effective engineering outcomes.
items.title: MIT Students Test AI's Role in Jet Engine Design Through JARVIS Challenge

key_points: MIT's Cybersecurity Clinic trains students to provide free cybersecurity assessments to local governments and healthcare organizations.
The program combines technical cybersecurity training with social science insights, focusing on 'defensive social engineering' to address human factors in security.
Students conduct vulnerability assessments, recommend protective measures, and help build organizational capacity for cybersecurity.
The clinic has completed over 40 assessments, with recommendations including software patching, multi-factor authentication, and ransomware response plans.
The course offers open online modules and has inspired similar programs at universities nationwide, with a consortium of 61 member institutions.
items.summary: MIT's Cybersecurity Clinic, launched in 2019, trains students to conduct free vulnerability assessments for municipalities and healthcare organizations. The program, led by Jungwoo Chun and Lawrence Susskind, combines technical training with social science insights, emphasizing 'defensive social engineering' to address human factors in cybersecurity. Students analyze clients' systems, recommend protective measures, and help build organizational capacity. The clinic has completed over 40 assessments, with recommendations including software patching, multi-factor authentication, and ransomware response plans. The course also offers open online modules, and has inspired similar programs at universities nationwide. Susskind notes that simple, low-cost measures can prevent most cyberattacks, and the clinic continues to follow up with clients for at least two years after each engagement.
items.title: MIT students provide free cybersecurity assessments to local governments

items.summary: Researchers at the University of California San Diego, with Google's support, are developing a low-carbon computing platform using retired smartphones. The project involves extracting motherboards from discarded phones and redeploying them as a general-purpose computing platform. This initiative aims to reduce the environmental impact of computing by avoiding the need for new hardware. The team plans to build a datacenter using 2,000 Pixel smartphones, providing low-cost cloud computing for students and researchers. The project will test the reliability of consumer-grade hardware under sustained use and is expected to launch in Fall 2026. The researchers note that smartphones, despite their smaller size, can perform similarly to servers in single-threaded tasks, making them suitable for certain computing applications.
items.title: UC San Diego researchers deploy 2,000 retired phones as low-carbon computing cluster

key_points: Google Research introduces Regularized f-Divergence Kernel Tests to improve auditing of machine unlearning.
Traditional two-sample testing often produces false positives due to retraining variations or residual data footprints.
The new framework uses f-divergences to detect subtle, localized data shifts that standard tests miss.
It reduces manual tuning and sample size requirements, outperforming existing methods in privacy violation detection.
The research highlights limitations of current unlearning techniques and proposes a relative three-sample test for accurate compliance assessment.
items.summary: Google Research introduces a new framework for auditing machine unlearning, addressing challenges in verifying whether AI models have effectively 'forgotten' specific data. The method, called Regularized f-Divergence Kernel Tests, enhances sensitivity and accuracy in detecting distributional shifts between models. Traditional two-sample testing often produces false positives due to retraining variations or residual data footprints. The new approach uses f-divergences to measure distance between data distributions, allowing auditors to detect subtle, localized shifts that standard tests miss. It also reduces the need for manual tuning and large sample sizes. The framework was tested on synthetic data and high-energy physics datasets, outperforming existing methods in detecting privacy violations with fewer samples. The research highlights the limitations of current unlearning techniques and proposes a relative three-sample test to more accurately assess compliance with privacy standards.
items.title: New framework improves auditing of machine unlearning

The initiative aims to study and mitigate risks from interactions between AI agents across different networks.

items.summary: Google DeepMind, alongside Schmidt Sciences and other organizations, is launching a $10M research funding call to address safety risks in multi-agent AI systems. The initiative focuses on understanding and mitigating risks from large-scale interactions between AI agents. The call invites global researchers to submit proposals by August 8, 2026, with results expected in Autumn 2026.
items.title: Google DeepMind Launches $10M Research Initiative for Multi-Agent AI Safety

key_points: Researchers introduce a method to train LLMs on diverse reasoning traces to improve decision-making.
Global forking tokens enable models to generate distinct reasoning paths during post-training.
Set-supervised fine-tuning (SSFT) pairs reasoning traces with tokens to avoid mode collapse and encourage specialization.
Reinforcement learning, specifically global forking policy optimization (GFPO), helps models select the most effective reasoning mode for each question.
The combined approach improves accuracy and reasoning diversity, outperforming standard pipelines while maintaining strong single-shot performance.
items.summary: Researchers propose a method to enhance large language models' reasoning capabilities by training them on diverse reasoning traces. The approach, presented at ICLR, introduces global forking tokens to prompt different reasoning modes during post-training. Set-supervised fine-tuning (SSFT) pairs each reasoning trace with a dedicated token, encouraging distinct behaviors and avoiding mode collapse. Reinforcement learning, specifically global forking policy optimization (GFPO), helps models select the most effective reasoning mode for each question. This combination improves single-shot accuracy and reasoning diversity, outperforming standard pipelines. The method maintains strong accuracy while increasing the likelihood of correct answers through diverse strategies.
items.title: New method trains LLMs to use diverse reasoning strategies for better decision-making

key_points: Researchers developed a framework linking architectural design to scaling laws for efficient LLM operation without accuracy loss.
The framework incorporates hidden size, MLP-to-attention ratio, and grouped-query attention as key architectural factors.
Surefire models achieve up to 47% higher throughput than LLaMA-3.2 on H200 GPUs while maintaining similar accuracy.
The framework is applicable across different hardware and serving systems, enabling cost-effective model exploration.
Optimal architectural configurations can unlock significant efficiency gains without accuracy cost.
items.summary: Researchers present a framework at ICLR that connects architectural design choices to scaling laws, enabling efficient large language model (LLM) operation without compromising accuracy. The study builds on the Chinchilla scaling law, which relates model loss to parameters and training data. The new approach incorporates three architectural factors: hidden size, MLP-to-attention ratio, and grouped-query attention (GQA). Each factor influences inference throughput differently, with optimal points for accuracy. The researchers developed two model families, Panda (maximizing accuracy) and Surefire (optimizing accuracy-efficiency tradeoff), through extensive experimentation with over 200 models. Results show Surefire models achieve up to 47% higher throughput than LLaMA-3.2 on H200 GPUs, while maintaining similar accuracy. The framework is applicable across different hardware and serving systems, allowing cost-effective exploration of model architectures before full-scale training.
items.title: Researchers develop framework to optimize LLM efficiency without sacrificing accuracy

key_points: NIST found wear and tear significantly affects PFAS levels in firefighter gear.
PFAS concentrations increased in hoods and gloves after abrasion and heat treatment.
Wildland gear showed decreased PFAS levels after wear and weathering.
The study provides a baseline for measuring PFAS in firefighter equipment.

items.summary: A new study by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) found that wear and tear significantly affects PFAS levels in firefighter gear. The research, published in May 2026, examined how abrasion, heat, and weathering impact PFAS concentrations in structural hoods, gloves, and wildland gear. PFAS levels increased in hoods and gloves after these treatments, while they decreased in wildland gear. The study suggests that wear may release more PFAS or alter its chemical form. NIST researchers note that these findings provide a baseline for measuring PFAS in gear and could help assess health risks. The study measured 56 PFAS compounds, focusing on those most relevant to health concerns. The findings highlight the need for ongoing research and industry changes as PFAS awareness grows.
items.title: NIST Study Shows PFAS Levels Change with Wear in Firefighter Gear

items.summary: Artificial Analysis introduced IFBench, a benchmark that tests how well language models follow precise natural-language instructions. Unlike other benchmarks, IFBench applies multiple constraints in a single response, reflecting real-world user requests. Declan Jackson of Artificial Analysis explained that IFBench was designed to fill a gap in evaluating instruction-following, which is crucial for practical AI use. The benchmark uses prompts derived from real user conversations, covering tasks like summarization and factual question answering. IFBench scores have shown improvement over time but remain uneven across models, with xAI's Grok 4.20 leading at 82.9%. The benchmark's openness allows for wide model testing and transparency, making it a valuable tool for assessing AI's ability to handle complex, multi-part instructions.

key_points: EMO is a new MoE model that develops modular structure through data rather than human-defined priors.
EMO allows using just 12.5% of its experts for a task while maintaining near full-model performance.
The model uses document boundaries as a weak signal to encourage coherent expert groups.
Benchmark results show EMO retains robust performance even with small expert subsets, outperforming standard MoEs in selective use scenarios.
EMO's expert clusters align with semantic domains rather than surface-level features, allowing meaningful task-specific subsets.
items.summary: Researchers introduce EMO, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model that develops modular structure through data rather than human-defined priors. EMO allows using just 12.5% of its experts for a task while maintaining near full-model performance. Unlike standard MoEs, which require all experts for good performance, EMO's modular design enables selective expert use. The model, with 14B total parameters, was trained on 1 trillion tokens and uses document boundaries as a weak signal to encourage coherent expert groups. Benchmark results show EMO retains robust performance even with small expert subsets, outperforming standard MoEs in selective use scenarios. The model's expert clusters align with semantic domains rather than surface-level features, allowing meaningful task-specific subsets. The researchers release the model, a baseline, and training code for further study.
items.title: EMO Model Enables Selective Expert Use with Near Full Performance

key_points: Schlamminger's team measured the gravitational constant with a precision experiment, yielding a value 0.0235% lower than a 2007 French study.
The discrepancy between measurements remains unresolved, despite rigorous efforts to eliminate experimental errors.
The experiment used a torsion balance, a method first employed by Henry Cavendish in 1798, and included checks with different materials to ensure accuracy.
Schlamminger, after a decade of work, plans to leave the problem to future generations of scientists.
items.summary: Physicist Stephan Schlamminger of NIST has completed a decade-long experiment to measure the gravitational constant, known as 'big G.' His team's result, 6.67387x10^-11 m³/kg/s², is 0.0235% lower than a 2007 French experiment. Despite meticulous efforts to eliminate experimental errors, the discrepancy remains unresolved, highlighting the challenge of precisely measuring gravity. Schlamminger's work, published in Metrologia, adds to the growing body of evidence on big G, though it does not yet resolve the mystery of why measurements vary. The experiment used a torsion balance, a method dating back to Henry Cavendish, and included additional checks with different materials to ensure accuracy. Schlamminger, who has dedicated years to the research, now plans to leave the problem to younger scientists.
items.title: NIST Physicist Measures Gravitational Constant with New Precision

key_points: Agentic AI systems are driving increased CPU demand due to their autonomous operations and tool use capabilities.
CPU-based tasks in agentic AI include parsing output, making API calls, and managing sub-agents, which are not efficiently handled by GPUs.
Researchers have identified CPU idle time during agentic AI workflows and proposed scheduling optimizations to reduce latency.
Tokenization, a key step in LLM processing, creates additional CPU bottlenecks, especially with longer sequence lengths.
Industry leaders like Intel, AMD, and Nvidia are increasing CPU production to meet growing demand, signaling a shift in AI infrastructure priorities.
items.summary: The rise of agentic AI systems, which operate autonomously and call sub-agents, is driving increased CPU demand, according to industry analysts and researchers. Unlike earlier AI workloads that focused on GPUs and memory, agentic AI tasks involve significant CPU-based operations such as parsing output, making API calls, and managing tool use. Matt Kimball of Moor Insights & Strategy notes that the number of agents can scale rapidly, leading to higher CPU utilization. Intel's Souvik Kundu and Georgia Tech researchers found that CPU idle time is common during agentic AI workflows, and proposed scheduling optimizations to reduce latency. Tokenization, a critical step in LLM processing, also contributes to CPU bottlenecks, especially with longer sequence lengths. Companies like Amazon, Intel, AMD, and Nvidia are responding to this shift, with Intel and AMD increasing server CPU production. Analysts warn of potential CPU shortages and price increases, similar to the GPU and memory shortages seen in recent years.
items.title: Agentic AI Drives CPU Demand as AI Workloads Shift

key_points: A Connecticut judge identified the first known use of AI prompt injection in US court filings by a plaintiff.

items.summary: A Connecticut judge identified the first known instance of a US plaintiff using AI prompt injection in court filings to influence a case. Matthew Elliott hid text formatted to be invisible to humans but legible to AI systems, aiming to sway the court's interpretation of his arguments. The judge noted the hidden text had no impact on the case's outcome but called the tactic a 'dangerous' precedent. Elliott faced sanctions for continuing to add hidden text despite court warnings. His later prompts included humorous and nonsensical messages, which he described as 'jokes'.
items.title: Plaintiff Attempts AI Prompt Injection in Court Filings, Judge Calls It a Dangerous Precedent

key_points: Raafe Khan highlights the economic mismatch between the cost of extending storage duration and the revenue generated in current market structures, using PJM's capacity pricing and BloombergNEF's cost curves as examples.

Captive batteries in data centers provide value through accelerated interconnection timelines rather than energy arbitrage, with their primary benefit being the reduction of opportunity costs from delays.
Khan identifies structural drivers like solar and wind buildout as key to battery storage growth, while cautioning about unpriced risks in cost decline assumptions.
He advocates for capacity market reforms, including multi-year commitments and aligned duration accreditation, to support long-duration energy storage deployment.

items.summary: Raafe Khan of Camelot Energy Group outlines the financial and market challenges facing long-duration energy storage (LDES) projects. He highlights the economic disconnect between the cost of extending storage duration and the revenue generated in current market structures, using PJM's capacity pricing and BloombergNEF's cost curves as examples. Khan argues that the market remains dominated by four-hour systems due to poor economic returns for longer durations. He also discusses the role of captive batteries in data centers, emphasizing their value in accelerating interconnection timelines rather than energy arbitrage. Khan identifies structural drivers like solar and wind buildout as key to battery storage growth, while cautioning about unpriced risks in cost decline assumptions. He advocates for capacity market reforms, including multi-year commitments and aligned duration accreditation, to support LDES deployment. Additionally, he notes the evolving role of merchant batteries and the importance of optimization strategies in a competitive market.
items.title: Raafe Khan analyzes financial challenges and market dynamics for long-duration energy storage

Local airlines have accumulated over 60 billion Naira in debt, forcing route cuts and price hikes. Analysts note that the issue lies not with supply but with the cost of transporting fuel to airports, involving multiple traders and high logistics expenses. Solutions proposed include direct government procurement from the refinery to reduce middlemen and stabilize prices, though Dangote's role as a global supplier may complicate such efforts.
items.title: Nigeria's Dangote refinery fuels Europe amid domestic shortages

key_points: Iranian lawmakers have proposed withdrawing from the NPT as a response to U.S. economic pressure.
Experts suggest such a withdrawal would signal Iran's intent to develop nuclear weapons or move closer to that goal.
Analysts argue that the threat of withdrawal is more strategic than a real policy, as it maintains ambiguity about Iran's nuclear capabilities.
Iran's stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium and reduced international oversight complicate the situation.
The international community would closely monitor any attempt to invoke Article X, as seen in the case of North Korea's uncertain status after its 2003 withdrawal.
items.summary: Iranian lawmakers have proposed withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), a move seen as a response to increased U.S. economic pressure. The proposal, submitted by MP Ghasem Ravanbakhsh, is being considered by officials, though its actual implementation remains uncertain. Experts suggest such a withdrawal would signal Iran's intent to develop nuclear weapons or move closer to that goal, potentially increasing international pressure and military risks. The NPT allows withdrawal with three months' notice, but analysts argue that the threat of withdrawal is more strategic than a real policy, as it maintains ambiguity about Iran's nuclear capabilities. Iran's stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium and reduced international oversight further complicate the situation, with some experts suggesting that remaining within the treaty while limiting inspections offers more strategic advantages. The international community, including the IAEA, would closely monitor any attempt to invoke Article X, as seen in the case of North Korea's uncertain status after its 2003 withdrawal.
items.title: Iranian lawmakers propose leaving nuclear treaty amid tensions

key_points: Up to 97.7% of deceased NFL players between 2016 and 2021 may have had CTE, according to a study in the British Medical Journal.
Of 235 brain donors, 215 were diagnosed with CTE, showing a higher prevalence than prior community-based studies.
Researchers attributed much of the head impact exposure to collegiate, high school, and youth levels of play.
The NFL stated it is committed to improving safety and providing health resources for players.
items.summary: A study published in the British Medical Journal found that up to 97.7% of deceased NFL players between 2016 and 2021 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease. Of 235 brain donors, 215 were diagnosed with CTE, indicating a significantly higher prevalence than previous community-based studies. Researchers noted that many head impacts occurred at lower levels of play, contributing to the risk. The NFL responded by emphasizing its efforts to improve safety and provide health resources for players.
items.title: NFL players' brain disease rates exceed prior estimates

key_points: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned U.S. sanctions on ICC President Tomoko Akane as incompatible with Japan's stance.
Japan urged the U.S. not to sanction Akane, a Japanese national, and pledged continued support for her.
Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi confirmed officials have met with Akane in the Netherlands and remain in close contact with her.
Takaichi emphasized Japan's support for the ICC and its role as a major financial contributor.
items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated Japan takes U.S. sanctions on ICC President Tomoko Akane seriously, calling the measure incompatible with Japan's stance. Takaichi emphasized Japan's support for the ICC and its role as a major financial contributor. She noted Japan had urged the U.S. not to sanction Akane, a Japanese national, and pledged continued support for her. Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi confirmed officials have met with Akane in the Netherlands and remain in close contact with her.
items.title: Japan's PM Takaichi Condemns U.S. Sanctions on ICC President

key_points: The Fire and Disaster Management Agency reported 41,174 heatstroke cases requiring hospitalization in July, the third highest since 2008.
Over 60% of patients were aged 65 or older, with 79 deaths confirmed.
The agency urged hydration, air conditioning use, and attendance at cooling shelters.
items.summary: The Fire and Disaster Management Agency reported 41,174 heatstroke cases requiring hospitalization in July, the third highest since 2008. items.title: Japan records 41,174 heatstroke hospitalizations in July

key_points: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions against Iran, framing them as an 'economic D-Day' to isolate the country economically.
The Supreme Court temporarily blocked a lower court's ruling against Trump's mail-in voting restrictions, which targeted 23 Democratic-led states.
Critics warn that Trump's mail-in voting order could create chaos for the midterms, despite the administration's claim it aims to prevent non-citizen voting.
While some Gulf allies have cut ties with Iran, China and others have criticized the measures as unilateral.
The Trump administration hopes for regime change to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, though Iran has prepared for the economic consequences.
items.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions against Iran, framing them as an 'economic D-Day' to isolate the country economically. The Trump administration warns that no entity is beyond U.S. sanctions and hopes for regime change to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons. While some Gulf allies like the UAE have cut ties with Iran, China and others have criticized the measures as unilateral. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court temporarily blocked a lower court's ruling against Trump's mail-in voting restrictions, which targeted 23 Democratic-led states. The court did not rule on the legality of the order, which aims to prevent non-citizen voting, though critics warn it could disrupt midterm elections. The decision highlights ongoing legal battles over voting rights and federal authority.
items.title: Trump seeks Iran isolation, SCOTUS halts mail-in voting restrictions

key_points: The MEAI praised the MMDR Amendment Act for enhancing clarity and stability in the mining sector.
Section 9D prohibits state governments from imposing taxes on mineral rights based on quantity, value, or royalty, except under central government conditions.
The amendment provides greater certainty for existing mining lease holders and reduces financial uncertainty for projects.
MEAI urged mining states to align their tax policies with the amended framework.
The changes are expected to benefit downstream industries like steel and cement.
items.summary: The Mining Engineers’ Association of India (MEAI) praised the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, for enhancing clarity and stability in the mining sector. The act introduces Section 9D, which prohibits state governments from imposing taxes or levies on mineral rights based on quantity, value, or royalty, except under central government conditions. MEAI secretary general M. Narsaiah noted that this provision offers greater certainty for existing lease holders and reduces financial uncertainty for mining projects. The association urged mining states to align their tax policies with the amended framework. The changes are expected to benefit downstream industries like steel and cement as well.
items.title: Mining Association Commends MMDR Act Amendment for Fiscal Clarity

key_points: TTD Board member G. Bhanu Prakash Reddy met Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to request accelerated work on the Chennai-Tirupati highway.
Reddy highlighted frequent accidents on the stretch between the Taj Hotel flyover and Peruru Junction.
The minister reportedly directed officials to prioritize underpass construction on a war footing.
The meeting occurred in New Delhi on August 25, 2026.
items.summary: A TTD Trust Board member, G. Bhanu Prakash Reddy, met with Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to request faster progress on the Chennai-Tirupati highway. He highlighted frequent accidents between the Taj Hotel flyover and Peruru Junction, a concern previously raised during Gadkari's visit. The minister reportedly instructed officials to prioritize underpass construction. The meeting took place in New Delhi on August 25, 2026.
items.title: TTD Board Member Requests Accelerated Work on Chennai-Tirupati Highway

key_points: Air India is seeking $1.5 billion in fresh equity from Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines to address rising losses.
The airline's combined losses for FY26 reached $2.33 billion, more than double the prior year's losses.
The funding request is expected to come in tranches, with Singapore Airlines contributing its share.
Air India faces challenges including a Pakistan airspace ban, international network disruptions, and the aftermath of a fatal crash.
Tata Sons' chairman has warned that the turnaround could take up to a decade due to supply-chain issues and systemic overhauls needed.
items.summary: Air India is seeking $1.5 billion in fresh equity from Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines to address mounting losses, according to two sources. The airline's combined losses for the fiscal year ended March 2026 reached $2.33 billion, more than double the previous year. The funding request, which would be one of the largest since Tata took control in 2022, is expected to come in tranches, with Singapore Airlines contributing its share. Discussions are ongoing, and no decision has been made. Air India faces challenges including a Pakistan airspace ban, international network disruptions, and the aftermath of a fatal crash. Tata Sons' chairman, N. Chandrasekaran, has warned that the turnaround could take up to a decade due to supply-chain issues and systemic overhauls needed.
items.title: Air India seeks $1.5 billion from owners Tata, Singapore Air as losses mount, sources say

The discussions focused on maintaining peace along the India-China border and advancing bilateral relations.
Doval met Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, who emphasized strengthening peace and improving ties across multiple forums.
Han highlighted recent high-level meetings between Modi and Xi Jinping, which have helped improve bilateral relations.
Both sides called for managing the relationship strategically, expanding cooperation, and addressing differences to ensure sustained development of ties.
items.summary: India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held the 25th round of border talks in Beijing, focusing on maintaining peace along the India-China border and advancing bilateral relations. The discussions followed a meeting between Doval and Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, who emphasized strengthening peace and improving ties across economic, political, and multilateral forums. Han highlighted the momentum in bilateral relations, noting recent high-level meetings between Prime Minister Modi and President Xi Jinping. Both sides called for managing the relationship strategically, expanding cooperation, and addressing differences to ensure sustained development of ties.
items.title: India and China hold 25th border talks to promote peace and bilateral ties

key_points: BJP and Congress MPs clashed during a parliamentary standing committee meeting on 'crime against children'.
Congress MP Ajay Maken submitted a letter seeking discussion on alleged police use of pellet guns and lathicharge against students during the July 20 protest.
Ruling party members opposed the discussion, leading to a ruckus in the meeting.
The incident highlights ongoing tensions between opposition and ruling party over police actions during protests.
items.summary: During a parliamentary standing committee meeting on 'crime against children', BJP and Congress MPs clashed over allegations of police use of pellet guns and lathicharge against students during the July 20 protest. Congress MP Ajay Maken submitted a letter seeking a discussion on the incident, prompting a ruckus with ruling party members. The meeting, reported by ANI, highlighted tensions between opposition and ruling party over the handling of the protest.
items.title: Ruckus at House panel meet: BJP, Congress MPs spar over use of force on students at July 20 protest

key_points: Lenskart's valuation faced initial skepticism but grew to Rs 1.15 lakh crore by 2026.
The company operates across a wide price range, from Rs 500 glasses to Rs 30,000 progressive lenses.
Lenskart's international business grew 38% with improved EBITDA margins.
Analysts maintain positive ratings, citing strong growth, margin expansion, and international scaling potential.
The company's full-stack retail model, including technology-enabled eye testing and backward integration, supports its growth.
items.summary: Lenskart faced initial skepticism with its high valuation, as critics questioned its business model and compared it to failed IPOs. However, the company's market cap surged to Rs 1.15 lakh crore by 2026, driven by strong performance and a diversified business model. Lenskart operates across price points, from Rs 500 glasses to Rs 30,000 progressive lenses, and has expanded its international business with a 38% growth. The company's full-stack retail infrastructure, including technology-enabled eye testing and backward integration, supports its growth. Analysts maintain positive ratings, citing strong same-store sales growth, margin expansion, and potential for further international scaling. The company's evolution from a retail eyewear business to a multi-faceted enterprise with a focus on eye testing and premiumization has reshaped investor perceptions.
items.title: Lenskart's valuation journey from skepticism to 1.15 lakh crore market cap

key_points: Canara Robeco's CIO argues large-cap stocks offer better value than mid- and small-caps.
Earnings acceleration in key sectors like banking and IT is needed for large caps to rerate.
Nifty 500 earnings grew 15% YoY in Q1FY27, signaling a recovery from an 18-month downcycle.
The fund's portfolio is split 46% large-cap, 40% mid-cap, and 11% small-cap based on company quality.
Mid-cap valuations are supported by strong earnings growth but face risks from high energy prices and inflation.
items.summary: Canara Robeco's CIO, Shridatta Bhandwaldar, argues that large-cap stocks offer better value than mid- and small-caps despite current investor favor towards smaller firms. He highlights that large caps provide a stronger margin of safety, though meaningful rerating requires earnings acceleration in key sectors like banking, IT, FMCG, and oil and gas. Bhandwaldar remains constructive on equities, citing a 15% YoY earnings growth for the Nifty 500 in Q1FY27, signaling a recovery from an 18-month earnings downcycle. The fund's portfolio is split 46% large-cap, 40% mid-cap, and 11% small-cap, with allocations driven by company quality and growth potential. Mid-cap valuations, while expanded, are supported by strong earnings growth, though certain sectors like hospitality and finance face risks from high energy prices and inflation.
items.title: Canara Robeco CIO Advises on Largecap Value Amid Smallcap Popularity

key_points: Kerala's Onam festival, traditionally tied to agricultural harvests, has been disrupted by a weaker monsoon and heavy rains, causing significant crop losses.
Farmers report losses of up to ₹40,000, with the state's Department of Agriculture estimating losses at ₹127 crores, though farmers say the impact is harder to quantify.
Many farmers are purchasing ready-made Onam feasts instead of preparing them at home due to damaged crops, marking a shift in local customs.
Flower production has increased, with farmers capitalizing on higher prices despite some damage, while the state is importing more flowers from Tamil Nadu.
Climate change is disrupting traditional farming cycles, with experts warning of more extreme weather events and the need for adaptation strategies.
items.summary: Kerala's Onam festival, traditionally linked to agricultural prosperity, has been disrupted by a weaker monsoon and subsequent crop losses, leading to economic shifts and changes in local customs. Farmers report significant losses due to heavy rains and flooding, with some losing up to ₹40,000. The state's Department of Agriculture estimates losses at ₹127 crores, though farmers say the impact is harder to quantify. As a result, many are purchasing ready-made Onam feasts instead of preparing them at home. Meanwhile, flower production has increased, with farmers capitalizing on higher prices despite some damage. Climate change is affecting traditional farming cycles, with experts warning of more extreme weather events. Adaptation strategies, such as micro-irrigation and climate-resilient crops, are needed but remain financially out of reach for small farmers. The festival's economic impact is also felt through rising prices of agricultural products, with some items seeing price increases of up to 100% compared to last year. The situation highlights the growing challenges faced by farmers in Kerala as climate patterns become increasingly unpredictable.
items.title: Kerala’s Onam festival marred by a weaker monsoon and subsequent crop loss

items.summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh vowed a 'surgical strike' against 'anti-national' forces at Jadavpur University, following clashes between Left-leaning student groups and the ABVP. Ghosh accused pro-Kashmir azadi activists of misconduct during visits by dignitaries. The SFI condemned the remarks as reflecting a 'fascist mindset' and vowed to protest against BJP influence on campus.
items.title: West Bengal minister vows 'surgical strike' against 'anti-national' groups at Jadavpur University

key_points: Small businesses face operational hurdles due to a new biometric verification mandate for SIM issuance.
CUTS International warns that the mandate could lead to higher costs for medium-sized enterprises and greater strain on micro-enterprises.
The regulation defines 'business users' broadly, requiring biometric verification for each end user of a business connection.
Experts argue that the administrative and privacy costs may be particularly difficult for small businesses, where SIMs and phones frequently change hands among employees.
items.summary: Small businesses face operational challenges due to a new biometric verification mandate for SIM issuance, according to experts. The requirement places additional burdens on small firms with high staff turnover and limited financial resources. CUTS International warns that the mandate could lead to higher costs for medium-sized enterprises and greater strain on micro-enterprises. The regulation defines 'business users' broadly, requiring biometric verification for each end user of a business connection. Experts argue that the administrative and privacy costs may be particularly difficult for small businesses, where SIMs and phones frequently change hands among employees.
items.title: Biometric verification mandate creates operational challenges for small businesses in SIM issuance

key_points: Police are investigating vandalism in Kolathur following a dispute over cake payment.
Two men allegedly under the influence of alcohol refused to pay ₹120 for six cakes.
The group threw stones at the shop and house, damaging parked vehicles before fleeing.
Rajamangalam police registered a case and are analyzing CCTV footage to identify suspects.
items.summary: Police are searching for a group of men who vandalized a shop, house, and vehicles in Kolathur after a dispute over cake payment. The incident occurred on Sunday night when two men, allegedly under the influence of alcohol, refused to pay ₹120 for six cakes. Maripandi, the shop owner, offered a reduced price, which led to the men calling associates to the scene. The group then threw stones at the shop and house, damaged parked vehicles, and fled. Rajamangalam police registered a case and are analyzing CCTV footage to identify the suspects.
items.title: Police investigate vandalism after dispute over cake payment in Kolathur

Promoter Piyush Somani stated protests were previously unaddressed but are now being considered.
The IPO aims to fund GPU and cloud equipment purchases, with the issue opening on August 28, 2026.
Analysts noted the lack of dedicated data centre stocks complicates market assessment.
items.summary: ESDS Software Solutions, a data centre and AI provider, included local protests against data centres as a risk in its ₹720 crore IPO filing. The company highlighted potential impacts on operations, reputation, and stakeholder relationships. Promoter Piyush Somani noted that protests were previously unaddressed but are now being considered, with plans to locate data centres in industrial areas. The IPO aims to fund GPU and cloud equipment purchases, with the issue opening on August 28, 2026. Analysts noted the lack of dedicated data centre stocks complicates market assessment.
items.title: ESDS acknowledges local protests as risk in IPO filing

key_points: Three family members died by suicide, leading to allegations of murder and forced conversion.
Suicide notes named Sheikh Sadiq Khan as the accused, accusing him of harassment and blackmail.
Police are investigating the connection between Khan's alleged actions and the family's deaths, including the husband's earlier death.
Khan was arrested after a five-state search and is currently in judicial custody.
The investigation continues to examine potential involvement of other individuals, including a driver.
items.summary: Three members of an Andhra Pradesh family died by suicide, prompting a criminal investigation into alleged murder, blackmail, and forced religious conversion. Police recovered two suicide notes naming Sheikh Sadiq Khan, a rifle-shooting coach, as the accused. The notes accused Khan of harassment, threats, and pressuring Sowjanya to convert to Islam. Police are verifying the claims and investigating the possible link between Khan's alleged actions and the family's deaths, including the earlier death of Sowjanya's husband. Khan was arrested in Meerut after a five-state search and is in judicial custody.
items.title: Family suicide investigation reveals murder and forced conversion allegations

key_points: A 15-year-old boy's body was found in a Delhi drain three days after he fell in while chasing a kite.
The family claims the search efforts were inadequate, with multiple agencies failing to locate him promptly.
Authorities acknowledged the challenges of the search due to strong currents and debris, but the family remains unsatisfied with the response.
The boy's parents expressed grief over his death, highlighting his academic achievements and artistic talents.
One junior engineer was suspended over the incident, but the family dismissed it as insufficient.
items.summary: A 15-year-old boy, Mithun, was recovered from a drain in Delhi three days after he fell in while chasing a kite. His body was pulled out by a JCB excavator on Tuesday. Mithun's family claims the search efforts were inadequate, with multiple agencies failing to locate him promptly. His mother criticized the authorities for not initiating the search immediately, while his father, who works in sewers, searched for his son himself. The family alleges institutional delays and demands accountability, with one junior engineer suspended over the incident. The boy's parents expressed grief over his death, highlighting his academic achievements and artistic talents. Authorities acknowledged the challenges of the search due to strong currents and debris, but the family remains unsatisfied with the response.
items.title: 15-year-old boy's body found in Delhi drain after 3-day search

key_points: H1N1 is the primary driver of the current flu surge in India, accounting for 98% of Influenza A cases.
Dr Bahl advises against mask-wearing, emphasizing hand hygiene and maintaining distance from symptomatic individuals.
High-risk groups are encouraged to consider the Northern Hemisphere flu vaccine, though it is not universally recommended.
H1N1 has evolved into a seasonal flu with annual mutations, and surveillance systems are tracking viral changes in real time.
items.summary: Dr Rajiv Bahl, director general of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), stated that H1N1 is driving a seasonal flu surge in India, with nearly 98% of Influenza A cases attributed to this strain. He emphasized that most cases are mild and manageable at home, advising against masks and instead promoting hand hygiene and maintaining distance from symptomatic individuals. High-risk groups are encouraged to consider the Northern Hemisphere flu vaccine, though it is not universally recommended. Dr Bahl noted that H1N1 has evolved into a seasonal flu, circulating annually with minor mutations, and is sensitive to antivirals like oseltamivir. Surveillance systems across 73 hospitals and 167 labs are tracking viral mutations in real time.
items.title: ICMR chief says H1N1 drives flu surge, advises against masks

key_points: Sebi barred Varanium Cloud Ltd and its promoter Harshawardhan Sabale from the securities market for seven years.
Sabale is ordered to disgorge ₹128.77 crore in alleged unlawful gains, while VCL must return ₹62.51 crore diverted from its IPO and rights issue proceeds.
Sebi found VCL misrepresented financial statements, including fictitious sales and purchases, and misled investors about a proposed ₹2,683 crore acquisition.
The regulator noted that VCL's share price surged after listing, and Sabale and his group sold shares during this period, making unlawful gains.
Sebi also penalized Raj Jagtani, proprietor of BM Traders, and Athos Capital Advisors for aiding the company's fraudulent activities.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has barred Varanium Cloud Ltd (VCL) and its promoter Harshawardhan Sabale from the securities market for seven years. Sabale is ordered to disgorge ₹128.77 crore in alleged unlawful gains, while VCL must return ₹62.51 crore diverted from its IPO and rights issue proceeds. Sebi found VCL misrepresented financial statements, including fictitious sales and purchases, and misled investors about a proposed ₹2,683 crore acquisition. The regulator noted that VCL's share price surged after listing, and Sabale and his group sold shares during this period, making unlawful gains. Sebi also penalized Raj Jagtani, proprietor of BM Traders, and Athos Capital Advisors for aiding the company's fraudulent activities.
items.title: Sebi penalizes Varanium Cloud and promoter for financial misconduct

items.summary: Iranian state media aired a video threatening Barron Trump, prompting the Secret Service to investigate. The nearly three-minute clip, broadcast by IRIB, included questions about where to kill the 20-year-old and references to his locations. It also listed Barron’s online accounts and classmates.
